title: Answering who-questions with ei kukaan
summary: To say nobody, use kukaan with a negative verb. Kuka tulee? — Kukaan ei tule.
prerequisiteSkills: Negative information questions with plural action verbs
objectives: Answer a subject who-question with nobody.
Use ei kukaan as a short reply or kukaan ei in a complete negative statement.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.
To say nobody, use kukaan with a negative verb. In these subject answers, Kukaan ei tule means Nobody is coming. Although the meaning excludes every person, kukaan uses singular ei in this pattern.
keyPoints: The question asks who; the reply must express that no person fits.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Ei kukaan is a natural short reply to Kuka tulee? (“Who is coming?”). A full reply gives kukaan + ei + the negative main-verb form. Do not translate nobody by putting ei before an affirmative verb form, and do not use plural eivät with kukaan here.
A natural short reply to “Kuka tulee?” is “Ei kukaan.” (“Nobody.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Kukaan needs singular ei and the negative main-verb form in these full replies.
